meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – private law is codified under the Civil Code of Quebec (civil law tradition) while public law and federal constitutional jurisdiction operate under Canadian common law principles
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA, entered into force 2014)
Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (1986, as amended)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union (provisionally applied 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (Loi sur la publicité légale des entreprises, RLRQ c. P-44.1), arts. 2.1, 15, 24, 50.0.1 and its regulation, requiring declaration of beneficial owners in the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2229–2322 governing société en commandite (limited partnership). Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA, S.C. 2001, c. 17) and FINTRAC regulations, including beneficial ownership verification obligations and Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) requirements.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access – beneficial ownership information is filed with the REQ and accessible to Revenu Québec, law enforcement, AMF, FINTRAC and certain regulatory bodies; general public disclosure of the full UBO chain is restricted, although basic registry data (name, legal form, address, officers) remains public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing (commitment certificate) of each corporate ultimate beneficial owner and of the proposed general partner, if corporate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the country of incorporation (e.g., State Administration for Market Regulation, SAMR, in China) or corresponding provincial/state authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the originating country (China is party to the Apostille Convention as of 7 November 2023); consular legalization is not required where apostille is valid

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address of each individual ultimate beneficial owner and director (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Government-authorized notary public in the country of origin (e.g., PRC notary office)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency / register of directors and shareholders (or equivalent) of the corporate UBO chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, registered agent, or company registry of the relevant jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or banker's confirmation of beneficial ownership and account history for the shareholder/general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder's or general partner's bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank seal/signature notarization + Hague Apostille (or certified consular legalization in jurisdictions not yet party to the Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Quebec-based registered agent or incorporator to execute the declaration of registration with the REQ
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed general partner or corporate UBO in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization + Hague Apostille + certified French or English translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening must be applied to all UBOs, directors, general partners, signatories, and beneficial owners holding 25% or more. Standard screening sources include: Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List; United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; FINTRAC PEP class definitions and heads of international organizations; and enhanced adverse-media search in credible international financial databases (e.g., World-Check). For a B2B marketplace targeting cross-border payment rails (Alibaba_Pay, Swift Wire), a low-risk standard tier applies, but the absence of any PEP match must be documented independently and kept in the pre-incorporation client due diligence file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online search and name reservation portal available at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/en/ (also known as the Québec Enterprise Register)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (RLRQ c. C-11), any commercial or firm name in Québec shall have a French version; names may include internationally recognized terms but must include a French generic element where the name is descriptive or comprises a non-French term. For legal entities and partnerships, a transliteration to Latin alphabet is permitted, but the partnership designation must appear in French: 'société en commandite' or the accepted abbreviation 'S.E.C.'. The English abbreviation 'L.P.' is not a substitute for the French legal designation in a Québec registration unless the name is used in English-language commerce together with a French version. All ancillary materials (articles, resolutions, POAs) must be accompanied by a certified French translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Québec / Canada (where used to imply a Crown or governmental affiliation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal of a proposed name, the REQ issues a written refusal notice stating the legal basis. The applicant may: (1) within 30 days of refusal, file a revised name reservation application without prejudice; or (2) submit a formal written request for administrative reconsideration to the Registrar using the same file number, attaching the refusal notice and providing arguments why the name satisfies the French language criteria and is distinctive; and (3) upon final refusal, seek judicial review before the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) within 60 days of notification. The reservation is confirmed exclusively in the REQ's electronic registry; the reservation period expires 90 days after approval and is not extendable beyond an additional single administrative renewal of up to 90 days if the original declaration of registration has not yet been filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as an address for administrative correspondence and mail forwarding, but it must be a physical place in Québec capable of receiving service of process and located in the municipal territory of the declared establishment. Pure mailbox or non-physical virtual addresses are not compliant with the REQ's requirement to indicate an actual establishment (établissement) in Québec. For a cross-border B2B marketplace, Revenu Québec may disregard a merely virtual office when assessing permanent establishment income and Quebec value-added tax (TVQ); the partnership should maintain an operational presence through remote management or leased commercial space if substance is to survive audit.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high initial risk: 35–50% estimated probability of an unannounced physical compliance inspection by REQ, Revenu Québec or Canada Revenue Agency within the first 12 months, given the cross-border B2B platform activity, the use of virtual-office addresses, and the presence of foreign payment rails. Annual recurrence probability thereafter is approximately 15–20% for a low-risk standard-tier entity if the office is actively maintained and filings are timely.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2186–2244, especially arts. 2236–2244 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 2, 16–26; Regulation respecting the register of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Direction de l’immatriculation, online at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d’immatriculation (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership) filed with the Quebec Enterprise Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital or statutory escrow fund is imposed on a Québec société en commandite. Contributions of limited partners are fixed in the partnership agreement and may be in cash, property or services; a notarial or bank escrow may be used voluntarily to secure deferred subscription obligations, but no deposit to a government account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the partnership agreement of [●] Société en Commandite (S.E.C.) is approved and adopted as the governing contract; that the registered office of the partnership is fixed at [address], Québec, and the general partner is directed to file its declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises; that the capital subscriptions of the initial limited partners listed in the subscriber schedule are accepted; that [●] is appointed general partner’s authorized manager for operational matters; and that [Name A] and [Name B] are appointed Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, respectively, with authority to execute banking, tax and licensing filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and reservation with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), online name-search and reservation service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search in the Quebec enterprise register to confirm availability and distinctiveness. File a name reservation request containing the proposed French or bilingual name with the mandatory limited-partnership suffix 'Société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' Provide the general partner’s identification or corporate status, pay the prescribed fee, and obtain the REQ name-reservation certificate before filing the declaration of registration.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name with mandatory 'S.E.C.' or 'Société en commandite' suffix
Corporate status certificate or identification document for the general partner
REQ online account credentials or service mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or queried, submit an amended request with a more distinctive element and, where necessary, a written consent from the holder of a conflicting name. Re-file within 15 days; the name reservation fee is not usually refunded but the corrected reservation may proceed without a second fee if filed promptly and no new fee is prescribed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Direction de l’immatriculation, online filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the REQ online service and select the declaration of registration for a société en commandite. Enter the partnership’s legal name, the registered office address in Québec, the identity and address of each general partner, the prescribed particulars concerning contributions, the powers and restrictions of general partners, and the duration if not indefinite. Where the general partner is a corporation, provide its existing registration number or certificate of status. Submit the declaration electronically and pay the filing fee. The REQ issues the registration certificate and assigns the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). Notarization is not generally required for registration, but a notarized partnership agreement may be maintained for third-party and banking purposes.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate issued by REQ
Proof of authority to occupy the Québec registered office (lease or sublease)
Identification and proof of existence of each general partner
Summary or excerpt of the partnership agreement showing capital contributions and general partner powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ returns a deficiency notice, complete the missing particulars and resubmit the corrected declaration through the online file; any late-filing penalty is avoided if the correction is made within the notice period. If the registry query is based on a legal interpretation dispute, file a written submission to the Director of the Registraire and, if necessary, seek judicial review after exhausting administrative remedies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of partnership agreement and initial governance resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private act executed by all partners and the general partner’s board; no government portal is used, but any public-information change must later be filed with REQ as a declaration of update.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a written partnership agreement governing capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, transfer restrictions, dissolution events and the scope of the general partner’s authority. The general partner’s board adopts the first board resolution approving the partnership agreement, fixing the registered office, accepting the initial capital subscriptions, and appointing the chief executive officer and chief financial officer. Maintain executed powers of attorney or signing-authority records for bank accounts and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Initial board resolution of the general partner
Minutes of partners’ meeting or consent resolution
Officer appointment letters and signing authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a financial institution or counterparty rejects the governance documents, execute a ratifying resolution or ancillary agreement confirming the officers’ authority and signatory powers. If the internal governance record conflicts with the registered public information, file an amended declaration of update with REQ before relying on the internal document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and government-account registration with Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (RQ) and the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — online business registration through Revenu Québec’s 'Mon dossier d’entreprise' and CRA ‘Business Registration Online’.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ issued by REQ, register the limited partnership for GST/QST, payroll source deductions and, if the platform employs staff in Québec, the CNESST employer account. If cross-border transactions involve importation of goods or services, also apply for an import/export account with CRA and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) as needed. The partnership itself is a pass-through entity for income tax, but it must file the required partnership information returns in Canada and Québec and issue the prescribed information slips to partners.
required_dossiers: NEQ and certificate of registration from REQ
Executed partnership agreement and initial board resolution
General partner’s corporate status certificate or identification
List of authorized signatories and their government identification
Canadian banking details for tax remittances
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec or the CRA refuses or delays the online registration, correct the identification details or attach the missing partnership records and resubmit. Where an account is locked, verify the legal representative via the respective government portal or telephone agent, provide a fresh authorization, and reapply before the filing deadline to avoid penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central bank and supervisor of payment service providers under the Retail Payment Activities Act, together with OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) for prudential bank supervision and FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) for AML/CFT and monetary reporting. Canada maintains no foreign exchange control authority and no exchange control statute; the Exchange Control Act was terminated in 1951, and the Canadian dollar is fully subject to IMF Article VIII convertibility obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account; no exchange-control permits, no capital-export restrictions, no mandatory CAD conversion, and no restrictions on holding foreign currency bank accounts in Canada. Profit remittance by a Quebec Limited Partnership is unrestricted from a treasury perspective, with the only relevant hurdle being tax compliance: non-resident partners are subject to Part XIII withholding tax (generally 25% on dividends, interest, rents, royalties and certain partnership distributions, reduced to treaty rates of 5–15% where applicable), and Quebec may impose its own provincial withholding obligations on payments to non-residents. CAD, USD, EUR and offshore CNH accounts may be opened and maintained freely, and funds may be remitted offshore without central bank approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio into CAD. Export receipts may be retained in foreign-currency accounts indefinitely; the only compliance obligations are standard corporate tax recognition of foreign income and FINTRAC cross-border electronic funds transfer reporting where transactions exceed C$10,000 individually or in aggregate within a 24-hour period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency CAD/USD treasury account with dedicated Quebec-based corporate banking desk)
Capital Escrow Account (bank acting as escrow agent for inbound capital injection or investor warehousing)
Operational Account (integrated Cross-Border Banking unit supporting US and China correspondent flows)
Operational Account (multi-currency sweep and FX hedging capabilities)
Operational Account (strong Asia-Pacific and inter-American correspondent network for SWIFT MT103 clearing)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for FINTRAC-registered international payment service providers and digital PSPs; Low for unlicensed offshore EU/UK EMIs. A foreign EMI may not lawfully open settlement or operating accounts in Canada without registration as a Money Services Business with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and, for Quebec operations, without complying with the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) money-services-business regime on insurance and money-services licensing. Schedule I Canadian banks generally refuse to inter-operate with, or settle for, unlicensed offshore EMIs, and the Bank of Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act framework (Royal Assent 2024, phased implementation) now requires registration of payment service providers engaged in Canadian payment activities. The recommended structure is to maintain primary CAD/USD settlement accounts at Schedule I banks and to use a FINTRAC-registered PSP strictly as a collection rail for Alibaba.com Pay pay-ins from China and other Asian markets.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal statute mandates physical presence; FINTRAC permits fully remote identity verification under the clear-and-independent identification methodology including reliable-source third-party matching, virtual notarization and split-verification techniques. In practice, however, premier-tier Canadian banks applying enhanced due diligence to a non-resident-controlled Quebec Limited Partnership typically require at least one in-person interview at a Canadian branch by the General Partner's Authorized Signatory, supported by notarized identification of all ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the partnership. Remote onboarding is commercially viable but subject to bank policy, requiring: the Registraire des entreprises immatriculation certificate for the LP, the partnership agreement, a certified register of general partners and beneficial owners, identity and residential proof of each material partner, and a bank-format declaration confirming no anonymous or bearer interests exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque non-resident ownership chain above the Quebec LP; inability to document natural-person ultimate beneficial owners at or above the 25% threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized organizational chart tracing every intermediate vehicle to natural persons; certified partnership agreement and Registraire des entreprises registration certificate; UBO register identifying all 25%-plus owners; passport copies; recent residential proof; constitutive documents and corporate resolutions of each holding entity; audited financial statements; signed declaration of no nominee or trustee arrangements covering the LP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound capital injection from Asia or other offshore jurisdictions via SWIFT wires, with size or velocity inconsistent with the declared ISIC 4791 B2B marketplace business plan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital contribution and subscription agreements; escrow instruction letters; source-of-wealth declarations from each investing partner; bank reference letters from top-tier originating banks; board or limited-partner resolutions approving the capital raise; audited or management financials of contributors; milestone-based business plan with projected transaction volume.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border B2B marketplace disbursement pattern characterized by high-frequency payments to third-country merchants (US, EU, China) and potential sanctions/PEP screening hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML compliance program covering customer due diligence, PEP and economic-sanctions screening (SEMA, OFAC and EU regimes), transaction monitoring thresholds and Suspicious Transaction Report protocol; designated compliance officer; merchant onboarding procedures; end-beneficiary declarations; sanctions and PEP institutional screening evidence; tax registration details and beneficial ownership attestations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through tax classification and non-resident partner participation triggering enhanced due diligence on the LP's legal substance, including any nominal general partner or agency-like wording.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from a Quebec lawyer confirming the limited partnership is validly constituted under the Civil Code of Quebec and is tax-transparent for Canadian income tax purposes; evidence of economic substance including Canadian office, records and operational oversight; CRA filings and Part XIII remitter registration where relevant; fund-flow description differentiating capital contributions, distributions and management fees.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital is SWIFT MT103 (for CAD and EUR) and Fedwire/CHIPS correspondent leg for USD, credited to the LP's CAD/USD operational account at a Schedule I Canadian bank. The remitter must pass full KYC with passport-level identification, tag 70 should state the clear economic purpose (e.g. Capital contribution under Limited Partnership Agreement, ISIC 4791 platform operations), and the originating bank must provide traceable intermediary chain. CAD-final clearing occurs via Payments Canada Lynx (RTGS); USD clears through New York CHIPS/Fedwire. FINTRAC cross-border EFT reporting applies only where the movement exceeds C$10,000 in a single transaction or within a 24-hour aggregate. No Canadian exchange-control permit or official purpose-code registration is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary outbound rails are SWIFT MT103 for commercial payments to B2B suppliers and Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700, typically sight LC) for high-value wholesale procurement requiring document-based settlement, with MT760 bank guarantees where foreign counterparties demand security. CAD disbursements clear via Lynx, USD via CHIPS/Fedwire, and EUR via TARGET2 through corresponding banking relationships. Marketplace payouts to Chinese merchants on the Alibaba.com Pay side are consolidated through a FINTRAC-registered PSP and reconciled in the treasury ledger before final reimbursement from the LP's Schedule I settlement account; digital CAD payouts to domestic merchants may use Payments Canada Real-Time Rail (RTR) where commercially available, with EFT fallback.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR and offshore CNH deliverable forwards) with authorized dealer banks of Schedule I standing and tenors generally up to 12 months
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in CNY for hedging onshore Chinese exporter receivables where deliverable CNH is not available
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) between CAD, USD and RMB/CNH for interest-bearing capital injections and long-dated treasury exposure
Vanilla FX Options and Zero-Cost Collars on CAD/USD and USD/CNH for asymmetric hedging of marketplace pricing risk
Exchange-Traded FX Futures on CME (CAD/USD futures and CNH/USD futures) as a transparent listed hedge overlay
Short-dated FX Swaps, Tom-Next and Forward-Forward roll structures for daily liquidity and clearing inventory management under ISDA/CSA collateral arrangements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual updating declaration and annual registration fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six months after the end of the limited partnership's fiscal year. File changes to registered information within the applicable statutory period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may incur statutory penalties and an additional fee; persistent non-compliance can result in loss of compliant status and eventual cancellation of registration. Fees are set in CAD and indexed; USD amount is approximate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (T5013), if filing criteria are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally five months after the partnership's fiscal year-end. Filing is required when CRA's partnership-return criteria apply, including specified revenue, asset, partner, or partner-type conditions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties may apply when a return is required; the basic penalty is generally CAD 25 per day, subject to a minimum and statutory maximum, with additional penalties possible for repeated failures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Quebec legislation generally does not impose an independent annual audit solely because an entity is a limited partnership. Audit requirements may arise under the partnership agreement, lender or investor terms, or other applicable reporting obligations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No single accounting framework is generally mandated for a Quebec limited partnership's statutory accounts. Canadian ASPE or IFRS may be used as appropriate to the reporting purpose; tax reporting must comply with applicable Canadian tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Review and confirm the partnership's registered information, including ultimate-beneficiary information, in the REQ annual updating declaration. Report changes within the applicable statutory filing period; do not treat annual confirmation as a substitute for prompt change reporting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors or managers, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 300–1,000 annually (approximately USD 220–740); service scope and provider rates vary.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No audit fee is statutorily required in the ordinary case; if an audit is contractually or otherwise required, an indicative range is CAD 3,000–10,000 (approximately USD 2,200–7,400), depending on complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate rate applied at partner level (Federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); the Quebec LP is a fiscally transparent partnership and is not a separate income tax taxpayer.
